label: Wednesday, October 28, 2026 · Fed-decision day edition
intro: Five finance reads to open the day. Headlines and two-sentence takes stay here; the full articles stay with the publishers. USC students read almost all of these free through the USC Libraries.

items.title: Fed decision day: hold expected at 2 p.m., Warsh presser in focus
items.take: The Fed is widely expected to leave rates unchanged when it announces at 2 p.m. ET, and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference will be watched for any hawkish bias. Tech stocks carry momentum into the decision after back-to-back gains for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq.

items.title: Microsoft and Alphabet report after the bell, with AI demand on the line
items.take: Two Big Tech giants and cloud leaders deliver updates on AI demand and their capex plans after the close. It is the other big catalyst of the day: traders want proof the AI buildout is still paying for itself.

items.title: DoorDash-Instacart deal could be finalized as soon as this week
items.take: The $17 billion takeover of Instacart's parent Maplebear could close within days, per the WSJ. Instacart was valued around $13 billion before the report, DoorDash is worth roughly $73 billion and saw shares drop about 6% Monday.

items.title: Anthropic picks JPMorgan to lead its IPO's US retail offering
items.take: JPMorgan will lead sales of shares to individual investors in Anthropic's potentially record-setting IPO. Routing a mega-deal's retail tranche through one bank is unusual and signals how hard the deal is chasing everyday demand.

items.title: DealBook: Who stands to gain from the Anthropic IPO
items.take: DealBook maps the winners and losers as Anthropic heads public, with Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley announcing a $63 billion deal to buy Broadcom chips for the AI company. Broadcom's CEO helped get the deal over the line over the weekend.

items.title: Podcast pick: The evolution of hedge fund performance, from enhancer to diversifier
items.take: This week's rotation lands on JPMorgan's Making Sense, on how hedge funds have shifted from return enhancers to portfolio diversifiers, a framing that maps neatly onto the AI concentration trade everyone is fretting about.
